claim: *Where Engineering Effort Moves.* As the fleet assumes work across the lifecycle, the engineer increasingly works through the surrounding engineering environment: specifying intent, choosing consequential abstractions, evaluating evidence, resolving tradeoffs, and adapting the environment itself.
topology: Unchanged five-phase lifecycle above three cross-lifecycle work bands; implementation emphasis retained without adding a new phase.
required_terms: Human engineering judgment\; abstractions; tradeoffs; acceptance; adaptation
Governed environment\ and context; permissions and constraints; evidence and validators; admission; operational controls
Implementation shifts disproportionately toward the fleet. Human effort concentrates where consequential judgment and responsibility remain.
bw_encoding: White ordinary nodes and groups; labels and boundaries carry roles without decorative tones.
redesign: Native nodes and routed edges preserve the original semantic structure, with print-sized labels and fewer decorative frames. Grayscale refinement: Human judgment, fleet execution, and durable environment regain separate bands; text preserves allocation distinctions. Fidelity pass: Restored within-band placement under lifecycle phases instead of collapsing responsibilities into centered prose lists; implementation receives bold emphasis in its own phase column.
alt: Across the top, the five lifecycle phases in order — Requirements, Design, Implementation, Validation, Operation and maintenance — connected by arrows; the lifecycle keeps its phases and gains no new ones. Below the phases, three horizontal bands show where the work sits. The human engineering judgment band carries intent, abstractions, tradeoffs, acceptance, and adaptation. The fleet band carries implementation, analysis, transformation, and routine remediation, with implementation emphasized in bold under its lifecycle phase. Responsibilities are placed under their corresponding phase columns. The governed environment band carries models and context, permissions and constraints, evidence and validators, admission, and operational controls across all phases. Implementation shifts disproportionately toward the fleet, and human effort concentrates where consequential judgment and responsibility remain.
